Main charitable entity types: NGO = company limited by guarantee (Companies Act No. 11 of 2022) with NGO status under NGO Act Cap. 315 RE 2020; domestic company at BCCAR.
Est. cost & time: BZ$100 (~USD 8) NGO application + incorporation ~BZ$250-400 (~USD 20-30); 1-4 weeks; a licensed local agent/registered office is required - agent fees add ~USD 750-1,500/year.
Key local requirements: 2+ directors (foreigners OK, no residency requirement), local registered office and company secretary via local agent; documents in English.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Local registered office and company secretary via Belizean agent; NGO license (AG's Office) for foreign-funded work.
Notes: English-speaking, simple Companies Registry; most expats form the non-profit company first and add charity registration later; local service providers handle everything. | confirm prior; standard vehicle is company limited by guarantee (Companies Act Ch. 250); charity status is a later AG licensing step | Verified: NPO status must be separately registered with the Attorney General's Ministry after incorporation

Main charitable entity types: Asociación sin fines de lucro (Ley de ONG's No. 894 + Reglamento, Registro de Asociaciones y Fundaciones, Ministerio de Gobernación); fundación; tax benefits via the MEF.
Est. cost & time: Registration fee ~USD 50-100 (SVC); ~1-3 months, exact time unpublished; a local office address is required; a foreign founder may participate with local co-founders on the board.
Key local requirements: Spanish-language articles, local address, registry filing under the 2011 Associations and Foundations Law; foreign founders permitted.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Spanish filings + local address; associations need resident members, foundations allow a single foreign founder via local POA.
Notes: Donor tax benefits are limited; NGOs receiving international funds should also register in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs NGO directory. | confirm prior; fundacion (Ley 2011) can be formed by one foreign founder via local counsel; donor donations are deductible, not 'limited'

Main charitable entity types: Fundación or asociación con personalidad jurídica (Ley Especial de Fomento para las ONGD, Decreto 32-2011), granted by the Secretaría de Gobernación, Justicia y Descentralización (SGJD) through DIRRSAC.
Est. cost & time: Registry fees modest (~USD 50-150) + notarial deed ~USD 200-500; ~15 days after a complete file; official fees unpublished; a local legal representative is required for foreigners.
Key local requirements: Spanish articles, local registered office, SGJD/DIRRSAC registry filing for associations and ONGDs.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): SGJD/DIRRSAC legal-personality filing plus local address/representative; all filings in Spanish.

Main charitable entity types: Asociación (Ley 218 de 1939); fundación (Ley de Fundaciones No. 5338 de 1973); fideicomiso — inscription at the Registro de Personas Jurídicas (Registro Nacional).
Est. cost & time: US$1,000–2,500 incl. notary; 4–8 weeks for registration, tax exemption takes months. Notary fee ~US$300–600; official timelines unpublished.
Time to register: 4-8 weeks (entity); interes publico decree adds months
Key local requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Personas Jurídicas; 3+ members for an asociación; a fundación's Junta Administrativa must include one member appointed by the Executive and one by the cantonal municipality.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Public deed before a CR notary + local office; asociaciones need 5+ members, so a fundacion (single founder) is the practical path.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación, asociación or corporación (personas jurídicas sin ánimo de lucro, Código Civil arts. 633-652) — registro ante Cámara de Comercio under Decreto 2150/1995 arts. 40-45 and Decreto 427/1996.
Est. cost & time: US$300–600 incl. lawyer; 2–6 weeks at Cámara de Comercio. Notary signature recognition (or optional public deed) ~US$50–150; official timelines unpublished.
Key local requirements: No nationality requirement for board; Colombian registered address; constitution by private document with recognized signatures (public deed not required) registered at the Cámara de Comercio; filings in Spanish.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (1+ founders) or corporación (5+ members) under Decreto Ejecutivo 193/2017 (Reglamento para el Otorgamiento de Personalidad Jurídica a las Organizaciones Sociales), registered in SUIOS via the competent ministry
Est. cost & time: US$500–1,500 incl. lawyer/notary; 2–3 months (Ministerio del Interior). Notary ~US$150–300; official timelines unpublished.
Key local requirements: Ecuadorian address and legal representative; Ecuadorian lawyer; registration in SUIOS with the competent ministry; ongoing reporting to the supervising ministry.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Resident president/board + local address, local lawyer; 2025 social transparency law adds registration & reporting
Notes: Foreign founders permitted as members/board; Spanish-language documents; IUP status adds time and a public-benefit declaration; banking and tax (SRI) onboarding is slow. | Prior context confirmed; 2025 Social Transparency Organic Law adds registration + foreign-funding controls (30% tax, suspension) | verify-rest 2026-10: Decreto 193/2017 governs; unverifiable 'Ley 2023-13/COEP' removed; ministerial grant carries no government fee

Main charitable entity types: Asociación (Código Civil arts. 80-98), fundación (arts. 99-110) or comité (arts. 111-123) — registro en SUNARP; fundaciones also register with the Consejo de Supervigilancia de Fundaciones (Ministerio de Justicia).
Est. cost & time: US$300–800 incl. lawyer; 2–6 weeks (notary deed + SUNARP registration). Notary ~US$150–250; official timelines unpublished.
Key local requirements: Public deed registered with SUNARP; local registered office; president/legal rep should be resident in Peru for banking; filings in Spanish.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Local registered office + SUNARP public deed; president resident for banking; Spanish filings; separate SUNAT exemption

Main charitable entity types: Fundación, ONG or entidad civil sin fines de lucro (Ley 351/2013 and DS 1597/2013) — personalidad jurídica from the Ministerio de la Presidencia (multi-department) or departmental Gobernación; cooperativa (Ley 356/2013).
Est. cost & time: US$400–1,000 incl. lawyer/notary; 2–4 months. Notary ~US$100–200; official timelines unpublished.
Key local requirements: Resident (Bolivian) officers, local address, notarized deed; foreign-constituted NGOs must sign a framework cooperation agreement with the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Ley 351 art. 13); Spanish only.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Resident officers + local address, notarized deed; foreign-constituted NGOs need a framework agreement with the Foreign Ministry (Ley 351 art. 13)
Notes: Foreign NGOs must register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería); 2023 law caps foreign government funding for certain activities and tightens oversight; heavy Spanish-language bureaucracy; few English speakers. | verify-rest 2026-10: registering authority corrected (not a 'Superintendencia de Compañías'); unverifiable 'Ley 1417/1475' references removed

Main charitable entity types: Non-profit company (Companies Act cap. 89:01); friendly society (Friendly Societies Act cap. 36:04); co-operative (Co-operative Societies Act Cap. 88:01 (1948, as am.)).
Est. cost & time: US$300–800 incl. lawyer; 1–3 months at DCRA. Filing ~US$100–300; official timelines unpublished; foreign nationals may incorporate.
Key local requirements: Guyanese registered office and resident directors; English is official; no citizenship requirement for board but a local presence is needed; no restrictions on foreign donations.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Guyanese registered office + resident directors; English official; no citizenship requirement; no donation restrictions
Notes: Easiest bureaucracy in the sub-region and English-speaking; non-profits face extra scrutiny at formation and take longer than companies; tax exemption is discretionary (Commissioner of Inland Revenue); friendly societies are the most common non-profit form. | Prior context confirmed; English-speaking, easiest bureaucracy in sub-region; tax exemption discretionary; Companies Act 1991

Main charitable entity types: Stichting (privaat nut) — Dutch-style foundation by notarial deed under the Stichtingenwet of 19 July 1968; also vereniging (association) and coöperatie.
Est. cost & time: Official fees unpublished (as of 2026); register fees set by staatsbesluit (Besluit Stichtingenregister G.B. 1970 no. 126, as amended). KKF excerpt SRD 300. Notary ~US$200–500, total ~US$500–1,500; 1–3 months (unofficial estimates).
Key local requirements: Surinamese notary (deeds in Dutch), local board/office in practice; 2013 Dutch-style Civil Code permits stichting with foreign elements but a local notary and presence are required in practice; Dutch language barrier.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Surinamese notary + Dutch deed, local board/office in practice, small legal market, banking requires local presence
Notes: Dutch is the working language — the main barrier; small legal market; banking requires a local presence; few English-speaking professionals; new Civil Code (in force 2013) modernized foundation law but practice is conservative. | Prior context confirmed; 2013 Civil Code modernized foundation law; notary deed + local presence required in practice | [verified] Stichtingenwet 1968 has no nationality/residence requirement for founder or board, and the seat is the place designated in the articles; but creation requires a notarial deed by a Surinamese notary, so a remote founder needs a notarized power of attorney; banking and practice favor local presence.

Main charitable entity types: Associação (Código Civil); fundação (Código Civil); OSCIP (Lei 9.790/1999) — registro em cartório de registro civil de pessoas jurídicas.
Est. cost & time: US$500–1,500 incl. lawyer/notary; 2–4 months (cartório + optional CGJ certification). Official timelines unpublished; foreigners may set up.
Key local requirements: Minimum 2 members (association) or 1 founder (foundation); Brazilian CNPJ and local address; notarial deed registered with a cartório; foreign founder may join the board; filings in Portuguese.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Local address + CNPJ, cartório deed, resident legal rep for foreign founders, bank account (câmbio rules); Portuguese
Notes: Heavy red tape (famous bureaucracy); main hurdles are getting a CPF and a bank account (foreign-inflow/câmbio rules); OSCIP certification gives donation tax deductions; 'instituição de utilidade pública' (federal/municipal) is a long, discretionary extra step. | Prior context confirmed; deduction is 6% individual / 2% corporate; OSCIP certification required for donor deductions

Main charitable entity types: Asociación civil y fundación (Código Civil, Ley 1183/1985); cooperativa (Ley 438/94) — plus mandatory National Registry of Non-Profit Organizations (MEF) under Ley 7363/2024 and Decreto 4806/2025; Registro Administrativo de Personas y Estructuras Jurídicas (Ley 6446/2019).
Est. cost & time: US$300–800 incl. lawyer; 1–3 months (MEF/DGPEJBF). Official timelines unpublished; foreign founders may register with a local representative.
